title: Oct 1 Results: Perfect Execution on the Mound
summary: Oct 1 recap: Went 1-0 with the Braves pick. Clean sheet from a pitcher's view.

content.value:
## Clean Inning, Clean Results

From a pitcher's perspective, there's nothing better than executing your game plan and watching it work. Today we went 1-0, and that Braves pick played out exactly how we saw it developing. When you trust your mechanics and stick to what the data tells you, good things happen.

## Breaking Down the Braves Win

The Phillies-Braves matchup was all about pitching dynamics and home field advantage. At 57% confidence, this wasn't a slam dunk pick, but the underlying metrics were solid. The Braves had the better bullpen depth and the platoon advantages we were looking for.

From my years on the mound, I know October baseball is different. Every pitch matters. Every matchup gets magnified. The Braves executed when it counted, and our analysis held up under pressure.

content.sub: 57% confidence · Home advantage played out perfectly

## No Games Tomorrow – Time to Reset

Just like a scheduled off-day during the season, tomorrow gives us time to analyze, adjust, and prepare. No games on the slate means we focus on refining our approach and getting ready for the next series of matchups.

In the bullpen, we used to call these days "maintenance days." You work on your mechanics, study film, and make sure you're sharp for when your number gets called. Same principle applies here.

### What We're Watching

With the off-day, I'll be diving deep into:
- Pitcher workload and rest patterns heading into the next slate
- Bullpen usage trends from today's game
- Weather patterns and field conditions for upcoming matchups
- Lineup adjustments teams might make with the extra day

Stay sharp. The next set of games will be here before you know it.

## Final Thoughts from the Mound

Perfect day at the office. You take these when you can get them, especially in October when the margin for error shrinks. The key is staying consistent with the process – trust your preparation, trust your analysis, and don't get too high or too low on any single result.

That's what I learned in my pitching days: stay even-keeled, execute the game plan, and let the results follow. Today, they did.

We'll be back with more picks when the games resume. Until then, enjoy the perfect record and the day off.

– Ace
